title.narrative: SCB ZamStats Increased availability of relevant statistics, 2025-2028
SCB ZamStats, Ökad tillgång till relevant statistik, 2025-2028

description.narrative:
Development objective
Official statistics is used to design policies for better living conditions in Zambia.
Project overall outcome
Enhanced capacity to produce statistics in line with user needs, sound statistical methods and international standards.
Component outcomes
Component 1: Management
Component objective/outcome: ZamStats has a leadership team that motivates and supports the staff to successfully adopt change in order to achieve the organisation's goals.
Component 2: Coordination
Component objective/outcome: A strengthened National Statistical System (NSS) that fosters stronger interagency collaborations to improve data integration, sharing, and dissemination across key government entities.
Component 3: Statistical Methodology
Component objective/outcome: Enhanced methodological capacity
Component 4: Economic Statistics
Component objective/outcome: Enhanced capacity for ZamStats to produce timely and relevant economic statistics.
Component 5: Agriculture, Environment and Social Statistics
Component objective/outcome 1: Agricultural and Environment statistics contributes to evidenced based decision-making on food security in the country.
Component objective/outcome 2: Household Budget Survey is produced to inform the users on critical socio-economic, agricultural and environment indicators.

Stöd till ZamStats för att stärka ledarskapet av ZamStats, samordningen av det nationella statistiksystemet samt metodologisk kapacitet inom ekonomi-, jordbruks-, miljö- och socialstatistik. Kapacitetsuppbyggnaden genomförs av Statistics Sweden. Stöd ges även till genomförandet av en årlig hushållsbudgetundersökning.

Support to ZamStats to strengthen the management of ZamStats, the coordination of the National Statistical System, methodological capacity in economic, agriculture, environment and social statistics. The capacity building is implemented by Statistics Sweden. Support is also giver to conduct a yearly Household Budget Survey.

description.narrative:
Examples of results achieved
Being the start up period, focus has been on consolidating and operationalization of institutional capacities at ZamStats and within the National Statistical System (NSS), putting earlier reforms into regular practice as well as planning for new areas of work. Capacity building and institutionalization of practices has contributed to sustainability and ownership, positioning ZamStats well for increased institutional independence.
Below there are examples of results and risks under each component:
Component 1: Management Component objective/outcome: ZamStats has a leadership team that motivates and supports the staff to successfully adopt change in order to achieve the organisation's goals. Within ZamStats, management practices became more structured. Planning and monitoring are now aligned with the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM) and followed up every week during senior management meetings. The results framework was further fine-tuned. The STAC course that was planned to be used to set baseline data in a few areas was pushed forward to Q1 2026, instead on Q4 as planned.
ZamStats struggled to prepare workplan, budget and agreement, so while the project started 1st August 2025 and an agreement with Statistics Sweden was signed, but the agreement with Ministry of Finance for channeling funds to ZamStats was not signed until midDecember. The first tranche of funds was disbursed December 23rd. No funds were utilised during 2025. The financial report and audit will cover 13 month, 1st December 2025 31st December 2026. The biggest challenge within the leadership component that will be followed up through continued dialogue is how ZamStats, with the support of Statistics Sweden will be able to handle the change management needed for a succesful operationalisation of the organsiational transition of the agency to fulfil its new mandate and increased independance. This will be followed through regular dialogue. There is also a need for a stronger internal coordination to handle the support from Sweden, that could be a leverage to further improve change management and team work instead of silos. This will be followed up by close dialogue and with an in-depth meeting in August 2026 to clarify expectations and agreement conditions.
Component 2: Coordination Component objective/outcome: A strengthened National Statistical System (NSS) that fosters stronger interagency collaborations to improve data integration, sharing, and dissemination across key government entities. Overall, ZamStats has continued strengthening its role as the coordinating authority for the National Statistical System (NSS) in Zambia. NSS actors increasingly cooperate instead of working separately. ZamStats monitored compliance with agreed producation and dissemination standards and a total of 24 institutions were monitired Q4 2025. A key result was the launch and operationalization of the National Data Science Training Hub in September 2025, which strengthened ZamStats coordinating role and shifted capacity development from ad hoc training to a permanent, nationally managed platform. The National Technical Working Groups continued to have regular meeting and the NTWG for Environment Statistic) started using the Hub shortly after it opened, showing a behavioral change toward shared spaces for coordination and learning rather than parallel, institution specific arrangements. There is a need to further enhance coordination with developing partners and to set up a clear structure and define roles within ZamStats to be more strategic with external support. The adopted strategic plan will serve as an important tool to enhance ZamStats leadership.
Component 3: Statistical Methodology Component objective/outcome: Enhanced methodological capacity No basic trainings took place during the reporting period. Internal work, especially to fine-tune the Cassava study methodology took leaps forward, with support from Statistics Sweden and the Swedish Board of Agriculture.
Component 4: Economic Statistics Component objective/outcome: Enhanced capacity for ZamStats to produce timely and relevant economic statistics. The work on rebasing the GDP estimations continued. There is improved capacity, with enhanced skills and confidence to work with the National Accounts Database (NADABAS) and stronger ownership from ZamStats together with COMESA to build capacity for the technical solution for NADABAS.
Component 5: Agriculture, Environment and Social Statistics Component objective/outcome 1: Agricultural and Environment statistics contributes to evidenced based decision making on food security in the country. Component objective/outcome 2: Household Budget Survey is produced to inform the users on critical socioeconomic, agricultural and environment indicators.
Progress on preparatory work on Agriculture and environmental statistics have been made. In agriculture, a clear plan for a Cassava Survey was developed, alongside steps to increase use of administrative data. In environment statistics, ZamStats and the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development jointly prepared and tested HBS (Household Budget Survey) questionnaire modules and agreed on next steps for an Environment Statistics Compendium, strengthening coordination and shared ownership. Regarding the Household Budget Survey (HBS), ZamStats has not been so progressive and is somewhat delayed. As it is a flagship survey for the country, the Embassy intends to follow the progress closely.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
